permissionsSection.onlyRepliesInsideAnExisting: Only replies inside an existing conversation, to its participants

permissionsSection.sendAttachmentsToSpeakrFor: Send attachments to Speakr for transcription

Your own actions are never gated. The first message to a new address always requires approval. An agent's read access is set by its token, not by these rules.
permissionsSection.actOnNotesYouForward: Act on notes you forward from your trusted addresses

phoneAccessAdmin.aHostNameOfIts: Use a dedicated host name, such as dav.example.com. Calendar paths must be at the root of the host. Saved when you leave the field or press Enter.
phoneAccessAdmin.letPhonesAndDesktopApps: Let phones and desktop apps connect
phoneAccessAdmin.offAppPasswordsThatUsers: Off. Users' app passwords are paused and work again when you turn this on.
phoneAccessAdmin.offEnterThePublicAddress: Off. Enter the public address first.
phoneAccessAdmin.onUsersMakeAppPasswords: On. Users create app passwords in Settings → Calendar & tasks → Phones and other apps.
phoneAccessAdmin.phoneAccessOffEveryApp: Phone access off. Every app password is paused.
phoneAccessAdmin.phoneAccessOnUsersCan: Phone access on. Users can create app passwords.
phoneAccessAdmin.usersCanConnectTheCalendar: Users can connect the calendar and contacts apps on iPhone, Mac, Android (DAVx5) or Thunderbird to their Mailr calendars, with an app password per device. Requires the DAV gateway and a host name on your reverse proxy; see “Phones and desktop apps” in the admin guide. Invitations made on a phone are not sent.

phoneApps.appPasswordDeletedTheDevice: App password deleted. The device can no longer sign in with it.
phoneApps.calendarNewCalendarOnThe: Calendar: New Calendar → On the Network, enter the username and {{url}}. Contacts: New Address Book → Add CardDAV Address Book, same address and username. Thunderbird asks for the password once.
phoneApps.downloadProfileForIphoneAnd: Download profile for iPhone and Mac
phoneApps.downloadTheProfileOnThe: Download the profile on the device, then open Settings and install it (on a Mac: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Profiles). Your calendars and contacts are added. The profile holds the password, so delete the file afterwards.
phoneApps.enterTheseInTheApp: Enter these in the app on the device. The password is shown only now; if you lose it, delete it and create a new one.
phoneApps.installDavx5ChooseLoginWith: Install DAVx5. Choose Login with URL and user name and enter {{url}}, the username and the password. Then pick the calendars and address books to sync.
phoneApps.itWorksAgainWhenPhone: The password works again when phone access is turned back on for your account.
phoneApps.passwordAnAppPasswordFrom: Password: an app password from the button above, not your Mailr password.
phoneApps.soYouCanTellThe: To tell passwords apart when you change phones.
phoneApps.theDeviceThatUsesThis: The device using this app password can no longer sign in. Its calendars and contacts stay on the server.
phoneApps.useYourMailrCalendarsTask: Use your Mailr calendars, task lists and contacts in the calendar and contacts apps on iPhone, Mac, Android (with DAVx5) or Thunderbird. Each device gets its own app password, valid for calendars and contacts only, never mail.

phoneAppsAdmin.anOlderNotesAppKeeps: Older Notes apps keep changes on the phone and show an update prompt. Empty: no limit. Saved when you leave the field or press Enter.
phoneAppsAdmin.everyNotesAppVersionIs: All Notes app versions are accepted again.
phoneAppsAdmin.everyVersionIsAnsweredMailr: All versions are accepted (MAILR_ANDROID_MIN_VERSION is empty).
phoneAppsAdmin.installNtfyAFreeNotification: Install ntfy, a free notification app, with Get ntfy during the app's setup.{{value}}
phoneAppsAdmin.noPushAppCheckedEvery: No push app (checked every 15 minutes, or a live connection)
phoneAppsAdmin.notesAppsOlderThanNow: Notes apps older than {{v}} must now update.
phoneAppsAdmin.nothingToTypePushWorks: Nothing to enter: push works at once through ntfy's server (ntfy.sh).
phoneAppsAdmin.notificationsAreEncryptedForEach: Notifications are encrypted for each phone, so a push server receives only the fact that a message arrived, never its sender or text.{{value}}
phoneAppsAdmin.phonesDownloadThatVersionAgain: Phones download that version again. The current version is kept as the fallback.
phoneAppsAdmin.pointNtfyAtYourServer: Point ntfy at your server, once. ntfy can't be set up by link, so the app has a Copy and open ntfy button: with one tap, people copy {{url}} and open ntfy, then paste it in ntfy's Settings → Default server.
phoneAppsAdmin.pushThenWorksAtOnce: Push then works at once through ntfy's server (ntfy.sh), as long as this server can reach the internet.
phoneAppsAdmin.signedInOnAnAndroid: Signed in on an Android app
phoneAppsAdmin.theAndroidAppsPhonesDownload: The Android apps phones download from this server, offered with version and checksum in the setup guide and on the Get the app page. Publish a release APK here or with mailr app-publish. The version is read from the APK; an APK of another app is refused.
phoneAppsAdmin.thisServerHoldsAnApk: This server has an APK of it, but its version can't be read.
phoneAppsAdmin.thisServerHoldsNoApk: This server has no APK of it. Phones are sent to
phoneAppsAdmin.toRunYourOwnNtfy: To run your own ntfy server, set MAILR_NTFY_URL.
phoneAppsAdmin.whatANewMemberDoes: Steps for a new member after signing in to the Mailr app:
phoneAppsAdmin.withoutNtfyTheAppChecks: Without ntfy, mail is checked every 15 minutes. People can turn on Live connection instead (Settings → Notifications) for instant mail with no other app, but Android then shows a permanent notification and uses more battery.

pictureSection.asksGravatarAndLibravatarAbout: Gravatar and Libravatar are asked about these addresses, so they learn them.
pictureSection.everythingIsInPlaceMail: Everything is in place. Mail apps that support BIMI show your logo once your mail passes DMARC.
pictureSection.forADomainYouOwn: For a domain you own, BIMI shows your logo beside verified mail in supporting apps. Only admins see this check. Remaining requirements per domain:
pictureSection.gmailOutlookAppleMailAnd: Your Mailr picture is not shown in Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail and other apps. They show these pictures for your addresses.
pictureSection.gmailShowsThePhotoOn: Gmail shows your Google account photo for {{emails}}. To change it, open <ext>Google Account → Personal info</ext> as that address and choose Profile picture.
pictureSection.outlookShowsThePhotoOn: Outlook shows your Microsoft account photo for {{emails}}. To change it, open <ext>Microsoft account → Your info</ext>, or <ext2>My Account</ext2> for a work or school account. Your organisation may manage that photo.
pictureSection.pngJpegGifOrWebp: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 2 MB. Location and camera data are removed.
pictureSection.shownNextToYourName: Shown next to your name in Mailr and {{name}}, and to other people on this server where your addresses appear. A sending address with its own picture (Mail → Writing → Send mail as) shows that one instead.
pictureSection.soOtherMailAppsShow: so other mail apps show it
pictureSection.someMailAppsShowThe: Some mail apps show a picture from Gravatar or Libravatar. Create a free account at <ext>Gravatar</ext> or <ext2>Libravatar</ext2>, add {{value}} and upload your picture there.

prepareUser.connectAMailAccountFor: Connect a mail account for them
prepareUser.connectedAtTheirFirstSign: Connected at their first sign-in, if their sign-in proves the address is theirs. They see “Connected by your administrator” and can disconnect it.
prepareUser.eachNewMemberOfThis: Each new member of this sign-in group (such as staff) gets these defaults.
prepareUser.leaveEmptyToKeepThe: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
prepareUser.mailAccountAtTheirFirst: Mail account {{address}} at their first sign-in
prepareUser.savedItAppliesWhenThey: Saved. Applies when they first sign in.
prepareUser.theGuideOffersGetTo: The guide includes an “About you” step (a few fields or a quick chat). Access to {{name}} still depends on their group's policy.
prepareUser.theLastScreenOffersTo: On the last screen: a shopping list, a note, and the Notes app on a phone.
prepareUser.theSetupGuideOffersThis: The setup guide offers this server with the address filled in. Each person signs in with their own account and sees their calendars and any you share.
prepareUser.usedOnceAtTheirFirst: Used once, at their first sign-in.

screenerTab.newSendersWaitInMail: New senders wait in <link>Mail → Screener</link>. When you turn it off, their mail moves to your Inbox.
screenerTab.screenAgainUndoesADecision: With Screen again, a decision is undone: the sender's next message waits in the Screener. Mail already moved stays where it is.
screenerTab.theScreenerKeepsMailFrom: First-time senders wait in Mail → Screener until you allow, block or label them. Never screened: people you have written to, contacts, VIPs, your own domains, replies in your conversations and invitations from known domains. You aren't notified about screened mail.
screenerTab.universityWorkAndLocalOnly: University, work and local-only accounts are not screened unless you choose them.

spamTab.learnsFromYourSpamNot: Learns from your Spam / Not spam clicks
spamTab.likelySpamFromNewSenders: Likely spam from new senders moves to Spam. Recommended.
spamTab.mailFromIsNoLonger: Mail from {{key}} is no longer sent to Spam.
spamTab.mailWhoseNameClaimsA: Mail claiming a well-known brand name (Facebook, PayPal, a bank…) but sent from another domain.
spamTab.mailrsOwnClassifierIsOff: The built-in classifier is off. Pick a level to turn it on.

spamTab.moveToSpamAtA: Move to Spam at a provider spam score of

spamTab.recordTheScoreShownUnder: Record the score (shown under “Why is this here?”) without moving anything.
spamTab.repliesToAConversationThat: Replies to a conversation that is entirely in Spam.
spamTab.scoreNewMailAndMove: Score new mail and move it to Spam when the score is high and the sender is new.
spamTab.sendersYouBlockAndFilters: Senders you block, and filters with a Spam or Never spam action.

spamTab.whenYouReportMailFrom_one: When you report {{marksNeeded}} or more conversations from one domain as spam within {{count}} day, later mail from that domain goes to Spam. Mail from people you write to is never moved. Choose “Not spam” or Remove to take a domain off the list.
spamTab.whenYouReportMailFrom_other: When you report {{marksNeeded}} or more conversations from one domain as spam within {{count}} days, later mail from that domain goes to Spam. Mail from people you write to is never moved. Choose “Not spam” or Remove to take a domain off the list.
spamTab.yourMailProviderFiltersSpam: Your provider filters spam first. These extra checks apply only to senders you have never written to or heard from; “Not spam” always takes precedence. Each decision is shown under “Why is this here?” on the message.

speakrSection.anyoneWithSuchALink: Anyone with the link can open the recording and its summary. You confirm each link, and {{name}} always asks.
speakrSection.connectYourSpeakrAccountTo: See meeting recordings, transcripts and summaries in Mailr, link them to events and draft follow-ups. Speakr is read-only unless you send it a file or turn on edits or share links here.
speakrSection.fromTheRecordingChangeThe: Change a recording's title and participants, or add to its notes. {{name}} asks each time.
speakrSection.hostedModelsMayNowRead: Hosted models may now read these recordings.
speakrSection.iMadeTheWebhookIn: I made the webhook in Speakr myself
speakrSection.inSpeakrOpenAccountSettings: In Speakr, open Account Settings → API Tokens → Create Token. Name it “Mailr”, pick an expiry (such as one year) and choose Integration access: read, write and upload. Add share only for public share links, and webhooks only for instant updates. Copy the token; Speakr shows it once. Older Speakr versions have no such choice: the token gets all your account's rights, and only what you turn on here is used.
speakrSection.inSpeakrOpenAccountSettings2: In Speakr, open Account Settings → Webhooks and create a webhook for recording events.
speakrSection.instantUpdatesOnUseSend: Instant updates on. Use Send test to check that Speakr reaches Mailr.
speakrSection.keepRecordingsAwayFromHosted: Keep recordings away from hosted models
speakrSection.mailrForgetsTheseRecordingsAnd: These recordings and their links to events, emails and tasks are removed from Mailr. Nothing is deleted in Speakr.
speakrSection.onByDefaultRecordingsHold: On by default. Recordings hold other people's voices and may include confidential meetings, so only local models read them. You can change this later.
speakrSection.pasteTheSecretSpeakrShows: Paste the secret from Speakr and choose Turn on. The address to enter in Speakr then appears here.
speakrSection.recordingsHoldOtherPeoplesVoices: Recordings hold other people's voices and may include confidential meetings. When on, only local models and local-only agent tokens can read them.
speakrSection.recordingsOtherSpeakrUsersShared: Recordings shared with you in Speakr appear with their owner's name. You can edit one only if its owner allows it.
speakrSection.recordingsSharedWithYouAppear: Recordings shared with you appear after the next sync.
speakrSection.recordingsSharedWithYouGo: Recordings shared with you are removed at the next sync.
speakrSection.recordingsStayAwayFromHosted: Recordings stay away from hosted models.
speakrSection.setUpInSpeakrCreates: Set up in Speakr: the webhook is created in your Speakr account and its secret is kept in Mailr.
speakrSection.speakrConnectedRecordingsAppearAfter: Speakr connected. Recordings appear after the first sync.
speakrSection.speakrIsAskedForChanges: Speakr is asked for changes every ten minutes.
speakrSection.speakrIsCheckedEveryTen: Speakr is checked every ten minutes.
speakrSection.speakrMustReachMailrWithout: Speakr must reach Mailr without signing in. If your proxy requires sign-in for all of Mailr, let /api/v1/integrations/speakr/ through. Speakr also refuses private addresses until its administrator allows them; the setting is named in the error message.
speakrSection.webhookOnInSpeakrSet: Webhook on. In Speakr, set the webhook address to {{url}}
speakrSection.withoutThisSpeakrIsChecked: Without a webhook, Speakr is checked every ten minutes. With one, new recordings, transcripts, summaries, deletions and edits arrive at once. {{pollNote}}

speakrWebhook.editsMadeInSpeakrsOwn: Edits made in Speakr's own pages still show at the next ten-minute check.
speakrWebhook.speakrReachedMailrTheTest: Speakr reached Mailr: the test arrived.
speakrWebhook.speakrReportsEditsMadeIn: Speakr reports edits made in its own pages too. A ten-minute check still runs in case a message is lost.
speakrWebhook.webhookOffInMailrSpeakr: Webhook off in Mailr. Speakr couldn't be reached, so delete the webhook named “Mailr” in Speakr's Account Settings → Webhooks.
speakrWebhook.webhookOffSpeakrIsChecked: Webhook off. Speakr is checked every ten minutes.

templatesTab.subject: Subject: {{subject}}
templatesTab.subjectOptionalUsedWhenThe: Subject (optional; used if the message has none)
templatesTab.textYouUseOftenIn: Text you use often. In a message, type ;shortcut and then Space or Tab, or use the Templates button. {{variables}} are filled from the first recipient and your sending address.

webSearchAdmin.aSelfHostedServiceSuch: A self-hosted service, such as degoog or SearXNG, on your network. Reached directly; its address must be private.
webSearchAdmin.anApiServiceSuchAs: An API service such as Exa. HTTPS only, through the egress proxy if one is set.
webSearchAdmin.anEgressProxyIsSet: An egress proxy is set (Image proxy below). It is used for internet providers and page reading.
webSearchAdmin.changingTheUrlOrThe: If you change the URL or service, enter the key again; otherwise the saved key is removed.
webSearchAdmin.countsOnceAnEgressProxy: Counts once an egress proxy is set under Image proxy.
webSearchAdmin.itsApiKeyIsDeleted: Its API key is deleted too. {{name}} uses the next provider in the list.
webSearchAdmin.noEgressProxyIsSet: No egress proxy is set. Internet providers and page reading connect directly from this server.
webSearchAdmin.noProvidersCannotSearchThe: No providers. {{name}} can't search the web until you add one.
webSearchAdmin.notAvailableThisServerDoes: Not available: private addresses are blocked (MAILR_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS=none).
webSearchAdmin.pausedTheEgressProxyIs: Paused: the egress proxy is required and not set
webSearchAdmin.sendQueriesThroughTheEgress: Send queries through the egress proxy
webSearchAdmin.testRunsOneSearchFor: Runs one search for “open source mail server” with these settings. Doesn't count against the limits.
webSearchAdmin.theProxyHidesThisServers: Hides this server's address from the search service.
webSearchAdmin.theServerRequiresTheEgress: The egress proxy is required (MAILR_REQUIRE_EGRESS). Internet providers and page reading go only through the proxy.
webSearchAdmin.theServicesSearchesTheWeb: Services {{name}} uses to search the web, tried from the top until one answers. Users get web search when “Web search” is on in their group's policy; admins always have it. Nothing from local-only accounts is put into a query, and every query is shown in the chat.

youSections.connectYourEmailChooseYour: Connect your email, choose your look, set up your phone and more, step by step.
youSections.everyNoteAndListAs: Every note and list as Markdown, with a JSON copy of everything, in one zip file. Export tables to CSV or Excel from each table.
youSections.shownToThePeopleYou: Shown to people you write to or share calendars and notes with. Each address can have its own name under Mail → Writing → Send mail as.
youSections.youFinishedTheGuideOpen: Guide finished. Open it again to change your choices.

pageReadersAdmin.desc: Readers for the web pages {{name}} opens. The built-in reader is always tried first. If it fails or returns almost no text (a page that requires JavaScript), the readers below are tried from the top until one returns the page's text.
pageReadersAdmin.fromTheServicesAddress: By the service, from its own address. It receives each page's address.
pageReadersAdmin.notUsedEgressRequired: Not used: it fetches from your network's address, and the egress proxy is required
pageReadersAdmin.fromYourNetworksAddress: By the service, from your network's address
pageReadersAdmin.browserThroughTheEgress: By the browser, through the egress proxy
pageReadersAdmin.pausedNoEgress: Paused: the egress proxy is required and not set
pageReadersAdmin.browserFromYourNetwork: By the browser, from your network's address (private addresses blocked)
pageReadersAdmin.deleteBody: Its API key is deleted too. Pages that require JavaScript go to the next reader in the list.
pageReadersAdmin.browserlessToken: browserless: the TOKEN set on the browserless container.
pageReadersAdmin.localDesc: A self-hosted service, such as browserless or Firecrawl, on your network. Reached directly; its address must be private.
pageReadersAdmin.internetDesc: A hosted service, such as Jina Reader or Firecrawl's cloud. It receives the address of every page it reads, and it fetches the page from its own address.
pageReadersAdmin.sendRequestsThroughTheEgress: Send requests through the egress proxy
pageReadersAdmin.hidesFromTheReader: Hides this server's address from the reader service.
pageReadersAdmin.readsAMinute: Page reads a minute (0: no limit)
pageReadersAdmin.readsADay: Page reads a day (0: no limit)
pageReadersAdmin.testReadsOnePage: Reads one Wikipedia page with these settings. Doesn't count against the limits.
pageReadersAdmin.browserDirect: By the browser, directly from your network's address (private addresses blocked)
pageReadersAdmin.setByTheServer: Set up by the server (MAILR_BROWSER_URL); the token comes from the server's settings
pageReadersAdmin.fromEnvDesc: This reader is set up by the server: a browser at {{url}} (MAILR_BROWSER_URL), with its token from MAILR_BROWSER_TOKEN. Here you choose its route, its order and its limits, and turn it on or off.
pageReadersAdmin.routeEgressDesc: Every page is loaded through the egress proxy (the VPN). Sites see the VPN's address.
pageReadersAdmin.routeEgressNone: No egress proxy is set, so pages are loaded directly until one is.
pageReadersAdmin.routeDirectDesc: Pages are loaded from this server's own network. Sites see your home address; nothing else changes. Private and local addresses stay blocked.
pageReadersAdmin.routeDirectRequired: Allowed while the egress proxy is required (MAILR_REQUIRE_EGRESS), because you choose it for this reader. The choice is recorded in the audit log.

emailLinks.confirmFirefox: Firefox asks you to confirm in a bar at the top of the page.

emailLinks.ios: On an iPhone or iPad, email links always open an app. No browser there can send them to a website.
emailLinks.android: On Android, install the Mailr app and choose it as your email app. Email links then open a draft in Mailr.

emailLinks.unsupported: This browser cannot open email links in a website. Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox for this.
